reference_line.info: Median of real cases, applied to Wisconsin: the median of the 24 repeal places changed by −0.50 permits per 1,000 existing homes per year against its comparison places. A repeal is not modelled as reducing permits, so it rounds to 0 added homes and coincides with "No measurable change" and with current law on the chart.
reference_line.label: Median of real cases

scenarios.info: Like the 24 US places that removed parking minimums for all housing: in the three years after, their permit rates did not rise measurably compared with similar places that kept them.
scenarios.label: No measurable change

scenarios.info: If the true average effect is at the top of what the evidence allows (95 times in 100, the real average would be lower): 2.21 more permits per 1,000 existing homes per year, everywhere except places that already have no parking minimums for housing.
scenarios.label: High end of the evidence
